title: I have finished the Face Contructor!!
content:
Yes, you read that right! I finally completed this project! I started it before my Eagle Project, so it had to go on pause for a while, but I'm glad I actually finished it! By the way, I am not liable for anything unethical done with it.

The way I am going to treat completed projects is simple, I will move them from the "current projects" tab to the "completed projects" tab and then post my full technical breakdown here on the blog. This is my first attempt so if you have any more questions or want clarification, post it in the comments and I will either respond here or update this post.

# Face Constructor: A Desktop Pipeline for Monocular 3D Face Reconstruction

## Overview

**Face Constructor** is a completed desktop application that uses an ordinary webcam to detect facial landmarks, reconstruct a 3D face surface, and export the result as **OBJ** and **STL** files. The project combines a PySide6 interface, OpenCV camera capture, MediaPipe face tracking, NumPy and SciPy geometry, and Open3D mesh processing. The source is available at [withereddetective/face_constructor](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor).

The user experience is deliberately focused: the app checks the camera, watches a live preview, requires the detected face to remain stable for three seconds, freezes one frame, reconstructs the mesh, and returns to the preview after displaying the exported file paths. This turns a technically dense reconstruction pipeline into a simple “hold still, capture, and export” workflow.

## Project at a Glance

- **Desktop UI:** PySide6 / Qt
- **Camera and 2D processing:** OpenCV
- **Face detection and landmarks:** MediaPipe Tasks Face Landmarker
- **Geometry:** NumPy, SciPy, and Open3D
- **Primary mesh topology:** MediaPipe face tessellation
- **Export formats:** OBJ and STL
- **Application entry point:** [app.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/app.py)
- **Core pipeline:** [3D-FaceReconstruction/main.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/main.py)
- **Runtime configuration:** [config.yaml](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/config.yaml)

No depth sensor or stereo camera is required. The result is monocular reconstruction: the pipeline infers relative depth from the 468 facial landmarks returned by MediaPipe, rather than measuring physical depth directly.

## Why This Is a Reconstruction, Not a Full 360-Degree Scan

The pipeline reconstructs the visible facial surface and a shallow closed backing, but it does not reconstruct the back of the head or unseen parts of the face. A long-standing README diagram may describe a broader or experimental feature set, so the implemented desktop behavior is the more accurate definition of scope.

The current geometry method:

1. Detects 468 points on the visible face.
2. Uses each point’s MediaPipe X, Y, and Z values.
3. Transforms those values into a normalized 3D coordinate system.
4. Rebuilds the face with MediaPipe’s canonical 852-triangle tessellation.
5. Caps open eye and mouth contours.
6. Adds a translated rear shell and side walls to create one closed mesh shell.
7. Optionally filters, smooths, cleans, and exports the mesh.

The code also includes experimental spherical, cylindrical, and planar UV mapping helpers, a Delaunay fallback, and optional MiDaS support, but the desktop app currently exports geometry without texture.

## System Architecture

```text
Webcam
  -> OpenCV frame capture
  -> Qt worker thread
  -> MediaPipe Face Landmarker
  -> 468 normalized landmarks
  -> exponential landmark smoothing
  -> coordinate transformation and face-scale normalization
  -> local depth-spike filtering
  -> MediaPipe topology or Delaunay fallback
  -> eye/mouth caps and closed backing shell
  -> optional Taubin smoothing
  -> export cleanup
  -> OBJ and STL files
```

The architecture avoids running the reconstruction loop directly inside Qt’s UI thread. `app.py` starts a `QThread` for repeated reconstruction and a `QTimer` for periodic camera preview updates. `FaceReconstructionWorker` shares the newest frame and latest detected face bounding boxes through separate locks, preventing the preview loop and reconstruction loop from stepping on each other.

## Desktop Capture Workflow

The desktop app begins in [app.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/app.py). Its `FaceWindow` opens OpenCV’s default camera, configures a 640 × 480 request, and creates a stacked interface containing the live preview, result page, and error page.

Every 30 milliseconds, `_update_preview()` reads a frame from `cv2.VideoCapture`. The worker may still be processing an earlier frame, so the preview is updated independently. The worker receives the latest frame through `update_frame()` rather than owning its own camera stream.

The processing loop then:

- Calls `FaceReconstruction3D.process_frame()` on the newest frame.
- Retrieves the resulting `TriangleMesh`.
- Converts normalized MediaPipe landmark positions into a pixel bounding box.
- Tracks the largest detected face through intersection-over-union matching.
- Requires one tracked candidate to remain continuously visible for 3 seconds.
- Changes the UI to a reconstruction state.
- Exports OBJ and STL copies of the captured mesh.
- Waits 4 seconds before returning to the preview.

Face tracking is intentionally generous: a new matching box must exceed only a 0.15 IoU threshold compared with the previously tracked box. When movement exceeds that threshold, the app starts a new stability timer rather than counting the first candidate’s full duration.

## Landmark Detection

[face_landmarker.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/face_landmarker.py) wraps the MediaPipe Tasks API. It initializes `FaceLandmarker` in **VIDEO** mode, with a default limit of one face and default detection/tracking confidence of 0.5.

The `.task` model is cached locally. On Windows, the cache is under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\face_constructor\models`; elsewhere it falls back to `~/.cache/face_constructor/models`. If no model is available and no custom path is configured, the app downloads MediaPipe’s Face Landmarker model once and atomically replaces a temporary download into the cache.

Each frame is converted from OpenCV’s BGR representation to RGB because MediaPipe expects RGB input. A monotonically increasing timestamp is supplied to `detect_for_video()`, allowing MediaPipe’s tracker to maintain temporal context.

## Coordinate and Scale Handling

Normalized landmark coordinates arrive in roughly the `[0, 1]` range. [utils.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/utils.py) converts them into world coordinates with these operations:

- Correct X and Z coordinates for processing-frame pixel aspect ratio.
- Center X and Y around 0.5.
- Scale X and Y by the configured `mesh.scale_factor`, defaulting to 10.
- Scale Z by `mesh.depth_scale`, defaulting to 10.
- Invert Y so that the resulting coordinate system uses an appropriate 3D display orientation.

The pipeline then normalizes face scale using a robust set of facial-border landmark indices. This targets a consistent face width instead of allowing camera distance or face size to distort the resulting mesh. The X and Y components remain based on the scan; no mirrored or averaged face replacement is used.

## Temporal Stabilization

Live landmark detections contain small frame-to-frame jitter. The pipeline uses exponential smoothing:

`new_landmark = 0.7 × current_landmark + 0.3 × previous_landmark`

This inexpensive filter reduces visible landmark noise while preserving most of the current frame’s measurements. Temporal smoothing is enabled through `stabilization.enable_kalman` in the configuration, although the implementation uses exponential smoothing rather than a full 3D Kalman predictor. The configuration key is an older or legacy name; it should not be read as implying that every Kalman feature in experimental modules is active in the desktop app.

The project also contains a [Kalman implementation](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/landmark_stabilization.py) and temporal smoother used by other pipeline components, but the main Qt capture path uses exponential smoothing.

## Depth Filtering

MediaPipe supplies Z values, but monocular Z estimates can include isolated spikes. [geometry_engine.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/geometry_engine.py) compares every vertex’s depth against the median depth of its canonical mesh neighbors.

If a point is farther outside the local distribution than a combined median absolute deviation and face-width threshold, the pipeline clamps it toward the local surface. This correction changes only Z values; it does not move X or Y coordinates or synthesize missing facial proportions.

The local threshold has a minimum size based on 2% of the detected face width, preventing tiny faces or flat depth distributions from producing arbitrary corrections.

## Mesh Generation

For 468 landmarks, `GeometryEngine` uses MediaPipe’s canonical tessellation. The module builds this topology from `FaceLandmarksConnections.FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION`, producing 852 base triangles.

This is preferable to a naive Delaunay triangulation for the face because the topology is consistent and stable across frames. Delaunay remains a fallback for nonstandard landmark counts or legacy geometry workflows.

After building the front surface, the engine closes three types of openings:

1. **Eye contours:** Contour loops receive central vertices at the median depth of their surrounding points.
2. **Mouth contour:** The same cap is applied to the mouth loop.
3. **Outer silhouette:** A translated rear copy, connected by side triangles, closes the outer boundary.

The rear copy is translated along the positive Z axis by 15% of the face width, capped by a minimum offset. It creates a closed, printable shell, not a learned reconstruction of the back of a person’s head.

The resulting canonical closed mesh has 942 vertices and 1880 triangles in the focused geometry test, and Open3D orientability, vertex-manifold, connected-component, and edge-count checks confirm that the test shell is structurally closed.

## Mesh Smoothing and Cleanup

The [main pipeline](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/main.py) supports Taubin smoothing, Laplacian smoothing, or simple smoothing through Open3D. The checked-in `config.yaml` deliberately disables live smoothing and refinement to preserve distinct facial features and avoid expensive cleanup every frame.

One smoothing pass can still be enabled by configuration, and mesh refinement can be enabled when an archival copy is needed. Export also performs a final cleanup independent of live configuration:

- Removes nonfinite vertices.
- Removes triangles referring to deleted vertices.
- Removes degenerate triangles.
- Removes duplicate triangles and vertices.
- Removes unreferenced vertices.
- Recomputes vertex normals.
- Rejects an export if the result is empty.

## Export Formats

[export_mesh.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/export_mesh.py) creates the output directory and writes mesh files. The desktop app changes `pipeline.mesh_exporter.output_dir` to the repository’s top-level `output` folder and exports both OBJ and STL versions of the same geometry.

The OBJ exporter writes ASCII geometry and can also create an MTL material file and PNG texture reference for textured workflows. The desktop call explicitly sets `include_texture=False`, so its OBJ contains geometry and normals rather than a captured face image.

The STL exporter intentionally omits color and textures because STL is primarily a surface-geometry format for printing and CAD interoperability. The repository includes PLY and GLTF/GLB implementations as additional pipeline capabilities, although the Qt workflow focuses on OBJ and STL.

## Error Handling and Thread Safety

The capture worker catches pipeline initialization, missing mesh, export, and cleanup failures and forwards human-readable messages through Qt signals. Examples include an unavailable camera, a stopped camera stream, an empty mesh, and a failure during OBJ or STL export.

The UI response is consistent: `_show_error()` stops the preview timer, requests worker interruption, switches to the error page, and avoids showing a success-shaped result. Worker cleanup calls `pipeline.cleanup()`, and the window close handler stops the reconstruction thread before releasing the camera.

Thread communication remains mostly signal-based. Only the latest frame and face boxes are shared, and both sets are protected with locks. The worker is isolated from Qt widgets and sends user-facing updates back with signals.

## Configuration

The checked-in [config.yaml](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/config.yaml) controls the camera, MediaPipe thresholds, mesh scale, smoothing, visualization, output directory, stabilization, and export settings. The current desktop configuration uses:

- 640 × 480 camera resolution.
- 640-pixel maximum processing width.
- A 10× X/Y scale and 10× Z scale.
- One smoothing iteration if enabled.
- Smoothing disabled for live capture.
- Refinement disabled for live capture.
- Exponential stabilization enabled.
- OBJ as the default standalone pipeline format.

A face above this 640-pixel processing width is downsampled before MediaPipe. The original frame remains available for UI display and bounding-box calculations, and normalized landmarks are then used against the processing-frame dimensions.

## Validation and Testing

The repository contains focused Pytest coverage for coordinate transformations, mesh topology, depth filtering, mesh refinement, video processing, utilities, and OBJ/STL export. A validation run with Python 3.13 completed **23 tests successfully and reported 3 failures**.

The failures are not evidence that the core mesh test suite passes universally. One test calls a missing `DepthEstimator.estimate_depth_from_landmarks()` method, one calls a missing `MathUtils.compute_distance()` method, and one coordinate test appears to expect a legacy absolute X centering of 5.0 even though the implementation centers normalized 0.5 at 0.0. These are stale API or assertion mismatches rather than failures in the reconstruction and closed-mesh tests.

The passing geometry checks include:

- Closed 468-landmark shell generation.
- 852 MediaPipe base triangles.
- 942 vertices and 1880 triangles after the current cap/backing construction.
- Every test edge occurring exactly twice in the closed shell.
- Orientability and vertex-manifold validity.
- One connected triangle component.
- Depth filtering that leaves X/Y coordinates unchanged.
- OBJ and STL file creation, including cleanup of NaN vertex data.

## Strengths

- **Simple hardware requirement:** a standard webcam is sufficient.
- **Strong desktop UX:** a clear hold, freeze, export, and return loop.
- **Stable topology:** MediaPipe’s canonical triangle structure avoids frame-to-frame connectivity changes.
- **Thread separation:** camera updates and reconstruction run outside the Qt event loop.
- **Closed output:** eye and mouth caps plus a backing shell provide a watertight export.
- **Feature preservation:** the pipeline does not replace the detected face with an averaged template.
- **Fail-safe export cleanup:** invalid vertices are removed before writing files.
- **Good modularity:** detection, geometry, export, visualization, and configuration are separated.

## Limitations

- The Z dimension is inferred from a 2D source and cannot equal true stereo or structured-light depth.
- The app reconstructs one face and uses the first detected face.
- The desktop app exports untextured OBJ/STL files, even though a broader texture pipeline exists.
- The rear shell is extrapolated geometry, not measured anatomy.
- Extreme head angles, glasses, occlusion, poor lighting, or low-resolution cameras can degrade the face landmarks.
- Smoothing and stabilization improve continuity but may lag or over-smooth fast motion.
- The repository contains experimental modules and legacy README/API assumptions that are broader than the desktop app.
- Performance is not published as a benchmark, so real-time FPS will vary by CPU, GPU, camera, and Python environment.

## Running the Project

From the repository root on Windows:

```powershell
python -m pip install PySide6 opencv-python numpy mediapipe open3d scipy PyYAML
python app.py
```

The desktop app creates the `output` directory automatically. When the face remains stable for three seconds, it writes timestamped `.obj` and `.stl` files and displays their full paths in the Qt result page.

The lower-level pipeline also exposes live, capture, and image modes from [main.py](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/blob/main/3D-FaceReconstruction/main.py), along with depth-map and mesh display options.

## Completed Deliverables

The repository now includes:

- A working PySide6 desktop application.
- Live camera preview and face-box tracking.
- A stability timer for capture decisions.
- MediaPipe landmark detection and tracking.
- A canonical 468-point face mesh implementation.
- Eye and mouth caps plus a closed backing shell.
- Temporal landmark smoothing.
- Local depth-spike filtering.
- Mesh cleanup and normal computation.
- OBJ and STL export.
- Unit tests and setup diagnostics.
- Desktop, pipeline, web, usage, and architecture documentation.

Example generated files are present in [output/](https://github.com/withereddetective/face_constructor/tree/main/output), including OBJ and STL captures.

## Lessons Learned

The main lesson is that reliable real-time reconstruction depends as much on timing and state management as on geometry. A beautiful mesh generated one time is not enough: capture must handle camera jitter, missing detections, face replacement, UI responsiveness, thread shutdown, and export failures.

The project also shows why a canonical face topology matters. A 468-point cloud needs consistent connectivity, and MediaPipe’s tessellation provides a much more stable front surface than rebuilding a triangulation independently every frame. The final closed shell also demonstrates the difference between a camera-plane visualization and a usable 3D artifact: a front surface alone is open, while export quality requires clean caps, finite vertices, consistent winding, and a connected shell.

## Conclusion

Face Constructor is more than a webcam demo: it is an end-to-end monocular face reconstruction system with a clear capture state machine, MediaPipe tracking, geometry processing, error handling, and standard mesh export. Its strengths are a stable, modular pipeline and a finished desktop workflow; its honest limitation is that it infers relative face depth from landmarks rather than acquiring true physical depth.

That balance makes it a practical portfolio project: it demonstrates computer vision, 3D geometry, threading, desktop UI, mesh formats, testing, and production-style failure handling in one compact application.

![some faces](./assets/scanned_faces.png)
Picture of the final result, first two are mine and the last one is of a friend.

Yep! So that was it, my Face Constructor! Have fun using it! (I will yet again reiterate, I am not liable for unethical use of this tool). Hey! Now I am going to pick back up work on this website! Woohoo! I have some ideas in mind... post here later!

-Withered Detective

title: I found out what to do with the Godot Multiplayer Project!
content:
So I did a thing...

Ok yes, you read the title of the post, I did it. It kinda works right now, at the computer science club meet it wasn't wanting to work across computers but maybe that was the district. It definetly needs further testing and development. I'm currently trying to get Henry to make the assets for this project so I can make it look better but I don't know if I want to continually work on a singular project for days on end. I like when I can think of cool additions to a project without having to worry about finding time to work on it, it gives me time to think of good implementation. That's kinda whats also happening with this website too. I don't know, but feel free to take a look at the game.

![the current game look](./assets/sticks_game_01.png)

You can find it in the "current projects" tab or you can just click the link right [here](https://github.com/withereddetective/godot-online-sticks-game). Its mostly the same low level networking code as before, I don't feel like giving a huge breakdown of it right here. Perhapds when I finish a project I'll make a whole post breaking down how it works. Anyhow, I will begin work on the face constructor again and I will hopefully finish it soon.

Unfortunate news from the Seguin Computer Science club, we will not actually do the Godot Wild Game Jam 99, none of us did any work yet so we vowed to actually do it next month.

But to end off on a good note, check out this game Henry made!

![Henry's game](./assets/henry_game_01.png)

He's been working on it on and off for a while now, its inspired heavily be Undertale and Deltarune but it has quite a few changes to stand out as well as his own cool artstyle! He wanted me to advertise it so I hope this is worth it! He's starting to do more projects so that's really nice. You can check it out right [here](https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/1210001511).

In other news, I am just on the cusp of getting my Eagle Rank! That's been taking a lot of my time... Anyways, thats all I have for now! Keep interacting with the blog! I'll respond whenever someone comments!

-Withered Detective

title: Addition to the First Big Update
content:
So I have just been having too much fun working on this website. I have been adding even more features such as:

- The ability to minimize and maximize posts
- A spinning donut in the top left corner of the page
- A whiteboard that says random messages when you click it

I will keep making new posts and I will respond to comments as much as I can, although I will refrain from just saying thank you to "oh this is so cool!!!1!" comments. However, I will pause on the updates to the site for now, I have other projects that I also want to continue working on, check the 'current projects' tab for that.

I would like to say one more thing though, please start commenting on literally any post besides the oldest one. Feel free to leave comments or suggestions on other posts too! Use this post for any issues or suggestions you want to bring up before the next big update!

But anyways, thank you for using this site.

-Withered Detective

title: First Big Update!
content:
This is the first big update to the site! I have added a few new features, including:

- The ability to lock comments on posts
- Audio credits for posts with audio
- A new plant that can be watered!
- Logging the amount of visits

Please try not to spam reload or spam the plant, while yes it is very hard to max out the use of firebase, it is nowhere near impossible. I hope this post is a good example of some of the newly added features.

I will continue to add more features as I think of them, and I will continue to post regularly.

-Withered Detective

content:

![the team again](./assets/hack_team.jpg)

Our project is called **"Missions to Mars"** and you can check it out right [here!](https://github.com/withereddetective/nasa-hackathon)
